title: Ingest backpressure SLI and trace linkage for Console usage pipeline
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a set of SLIs that measure ingest-side backpressure and partial drop behavior for the Console usage analytics pipeline, and ensure end-to-end trace linkage from API request -> producer -> broker -> consumer -> write to analytics store (clickhouse/pulsar/ksql as applicable).

Context: Recent spikes during onboarding demos (incident 2025-10-28) exposed that ~0.7% of usage events hit transient backpressure in the ingest tier and were retried multiple times, which increased p99 latencies and inflated token-cost estimations. Existing SLIs measure consumer write latency and consumer errors, but we lack an ingest-side backpressure SLI and reliable trace-id propagation across producers and brokers. That gap makes root-cause analysis slow and leads to overprovisioning.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Implement a new SLI: ingest_backpressure_rate = number of events encountering producer-side backpressure or broker-proxy throttling / total events ingested; target SLO: 0.2% monthly with alerting at 0.5% over 30m.
- Add a p99/p50 commit-latency SLI for the producer path (time from request received by Console API to offset acknowledged by broker).
- Ensure trace_id propagation: API request trace -> attach to Kafka message header (x-trace-id) -> consumer reads header and attaches to consumer trace/span so the full waterfall shows in Grafana/Tempo.
- Provide a Grafana dashboard (new tab in console-ingest observability) showing: ingest_backpressure_rate, producer_commit_latency p50/p95/p99, message_retries, and trace-link success rate (% messages with x-trace-id).
- Add a lightweight synthetic test that simulates a 500 rps burst with varying event sizes to validate SLI computation and alerting behavior in staging.
- Document runbook for paging and mitigation (auto-scaling knobs, temporary increased producer retries, consumer catch-up policy).

Technical approach and tradeoffs:
1) Instrumentation: Modify the Console API producer client to record a metric when it detects broker backpressure (e.g., producer.send returned with backpressure/error or linger time > threshold). We will emit a tagged counter (reason=broker_backpressure|producer_buffer_full|network_retry). This is cheap and explains partial drops.
2) Trace propagation: Use existing trace id from OpenTelemetry/Jaeger in API spans. When encoding messages, write trace id into kafka headers (key x-trace-id, value hex) and ensure our consumers read and attach span context. Tradeoff: adding headers increases message size; but header is small (~16 bytes). We will gate header propagation behind a feature flag to roll out gradually.
3) SLI calculation: Implement an aggregator job in the metrics pipeline (analytics-metrics-service) that reads producer counters and total ingested events per tenant and emits the ingest_backpressure_rate per-tenant and global. This keeps compute out of the hot path but relies on near-real-time metrics (1m granularity).
4) Sampling and fidelity: For high-cardinality tenants we cannot trace every event; we'll compute a trace-link success rate metric and sample 1% of events for full end-to-end traces. Adjust sampling in response to observed coverage.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: add producer metrics and header write (feature-flagged); update SDKs and API codepaths. Unit tests covering header serialization and metrics emission. (ENG changes, PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console-proxy/pull/2289)
- Week 2: consumer header extraction and trace attach; update consumer libs; integration tests in staging. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-consumers/pull/1045)
- Week 3: metrics aggregation job change + Grafana dashboard + alert rule in Alertmanager. Add synthetic test harness. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-metrics/pull/731)
- Week 4: staged rollout via feature flag, monitor and adjust SLO thresholds. Update runbook and notify SRE/Oncall.

Risks and mitigations:
- Overhead on producers: metric emission and header writes are minimal; if we see CPU pressure, rollback feature flag and use a dedicated sidecar to enrich headers.
- Missing header propagation due to intermediate proxies: we will validate end-to-end in staging and add middleware in proxies to preserve headers.
- Alert noise for tenants generating small volumes: alert on aggregated and tenant thresholds (minimum volume gating).

Acceptance tests:
- Synthetic burst test shows ingest_backpressure_rate < 0.5% under configured autoscale in staging.
- End-to-end trace demonstrates the same trace id across Console API -> Kafka -> Consumer -> Clickhouse write (trace visible in Tempo/Grafana for sampled events).
- Dashboard panels populated and alert fires when we artificially raise backpressure counter.

Deliverables:
- Code changes across console-proxy, ingest-consumers, analytics-metrics-service (links below).
- Grafana dashboard and Alertmanager rules.
- Runbook and run deck stored in Confluence.
